lab.title: Simulator Lab
lab.intro: Live demos of the simulation engine as it is built. Everything runs in your browser.

scenarioHint.line-follower: Arduino Uno + L298N + two TT motors + 3-channel line sensor on 4×AA. The firmware follows the black line around the oval.
scenarioHint.blink: The Uno toggles D13 every 500 ms through a 220 Ω resistor.
scenarioHint.button: Hold the button: D2 reads LOW through the internal pull-up and the sketch turns the LED on.
scenarioHint.dimmer: Turn the knob: analogRead(A0) sets the PWM duty on D6.
scenarioHint.servo: Turn the knob: the sketch maps A0 to the servo pulse width on D9. The servo runs from its own 4×AA pack — a stalled SG90 needs more than the Uno's 5 V pin can give.
scenarioHint.led-no-resistor: An LED straight on D13 with no resistor. The checker flags it before you run; run it and watch the pin and the LED burn out.
scenarioHint.outputs-fighting: D2 and D3 are wired together; the sketch drives D2 HIGH and D3 LOW — a short circuit through both pins.
scenarioHint.motor-on-pin: A TT motor straight on D9. Motors need a driver: the pin cannot supply the current.
scenarioHint.floating-input: A button on D2 to GND, but the sketch uses INPUT without a pull-up: released, the pin floats.
scenarioHint.serial: The sketch prints a greeting and a tick every second over Serial at 115200 baud, and echoes what you send in capitals (D13 toggles on every byte).
scenarioHint.rgb-melody: Turn the knob: the RGB LED walks the colour wheel with PWM on D9/D6/D5. Hold the button: tone() plays a melody on the passive buzzer on D8 (turn on Sound to hear it).
scenarioHint.relay-counter: Press the button to count 0–9 on the 7-segment display. On even numbers the relay closes and the 9 V battery lights the lamp through an LM7805 — a separate circuit the Uno only switches.
scenarioHint.half-adder: Press the buttons: a 74HC86 XOR makes the sum and a 74HC08 AND the carry, in hardware. The Uno only reads the result and prints it to the serial monitor.
scenarioHint.led-bar: A lit LED sweeps back and forth across 8 LEDs. shiftOut() clocks each pattern into a 74HC595, which drives the LEDs from just three Uno pins. The knob sets the speed.
scenarioHint.stepper-knob: Turn the knob: the 28BYJ-48 shaft follows it, one knob turn per shaft turn (2048 steps). The Stepper library drives the coils through a ULN2003A, because a pin cannot supply coil current.
scenarioHint.motor-driver: Two TT motors on a TB6612FNG MOSFET driver ramp from full reverse to full forward. STBY must be HIGH, or the driver sleeps. MOSFETs waste less voltage than the L298N.
scenarioHint.bump-avoider: Two lever switches at the front corners: when one hits an obstacle the robot backs up, turns away, and later turns back, working its way to the goal of the obstacle course.
scenarioHint.keypad-lock: Click the keys on the keypad: type 1234 then # to unlock (green LED); * clears. The Keypad library scans the rows and columns, and the serial monitor shows what you typed.
scenarioHint.input-devices: Turn the rotary encoder (its slider sets the knob position) and move the joystick: the sketch counts detents from the quadrature contacts and prints both to the serial monitor.
scenarioHint.timer-555: An NE555 timer blinks the LED about once a second all by itself: R1, R2 and the 10 µF capacitor set the rhythm (f = 1.44 / ((R1 + 2·R2)·C)). The Uno only listens on D2 and prints the period it measures.
scenarioHint.rc-charge: D7 charges a 100 µF capacitor through 10 kΩ and A0 watches it rise: 63 % of 5 V after one time constant (R·C = 1 s), almost full after five. Every 4 s the pin flips and it discharges. Watch the numbers in the serial monitor.
scenarioHint.transistor-motor: Turn the knob: the PWM duty on D9 switches a TIP120 Darlington, which carries the motor current from the 4×AA pack (a pin could not). The 1N4007 across the motor catches the coil's current every time the transistor switches off.
scenarioHint.mosfet-ramp: An IRLZ44N logic-level MOSFET, fully on with 5 V on its gate, ramps the motor up over 2 s, runs it, ramps it down and rests. 220 Ω limits the gate charging current; 10 kΩ keeps the gate low while the Uno boots.
scenarioHint.no-flyback: The same TIP120 motor switch, but without the diode. The checker flags it before you run. Run it: each time the PWM switches the motor off, its coil kicks the collector up to 60 V until the transistor breaks down, and soon it fails.
scenarioHint.laser-avoider: A VL53L0X time-of-flight sensor on the front measures the gap ahead with an infrared laser. Something within 45 cm: the robot veers right; with a clear view it veers back left until it has undone its turns, so it works its way to the goal. It talks I²C on A4/A5; XSHUT on D11 lets the sketch reset it.
scenarioHint.maze-solver: Three HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors look ahead, left and right. In the middle of each cell the robot turns right if it can, else goes straight, else left, else turns around: keeping its right hand on the wall leads it through the 5 × 5 maze to the goal. Between cells it steers to the middle of the corridor, and the front sensor measures how far it has driven.
scenarioHint.sumo-bot: An HC-SR04 on the front spins around looking for the opponent and charges anything within 60 cm; farther echoes are the arena walls. The line sensor, facing down, sees the white edge of the black ring: the robot backs off and turns, so it pushes the block out without leaving the ring itself.
scenarioHint.oled-knob: Turn the knob: the Adafruit_SSD1306 library draws the title, the reading and a bar into a 1 KB frame buffer in the Uno's RAM and sends it to the 128×64 OLED over I²C (A4/A5, address 0x3C) ten times a second.
scenarioHint.lcd-hello: A 16×2 character LCD driven through a PCF8574 I²C backpack: only two data wires instead of six. The sketch defines a heart as a custom character and counts the seconds on the second line. Turn the contrast knob if the text fades.
scenarioHint.imu-tilt: Tilt the MPU-6050 (its sliders set the angles) and watch the serial monitor: the sketch works out the tilt from gravity on the three axes and lights the LED past 20°. The gyroscope reports how fast it turns.
scenarioHint.weather-station: A BMP280 on the Uno's 3.3 V pin: it is a 3.3 V chip, so its module pulls the bus up to 3.3 V and the sketch switches off the Uno's own 5 V pull-ups after Wire starts. Change the temperature and altitude sliders and watch the readings follow (the IIR filter smooths them).
scenarioHint.thermometers: A DHT11 on D2 and a DS18B20 on D4, read every 2 s. Both talk over a single wire with precisely timed pulses: the DHT11 answers a 20 ms start pulse with 40 bits, the DS18B20 speaks 1-Wire and needs the 4.7 kΩ pull-up. Change their temperature sliders and compare: the DS18B20 resolves 1/16 °C, the DHT11 whole degrees.
scenarioHint.neopixel-rainbow: Eight WS2812B LEDs on D6 take their colours as 800 kHz pulses: a short HIGH is a 0, a long one a 1, 24 bits per LED, passed along the strip. Turn the knob for brightness. Each LED draws up to 36 mA at full white, so long strips need their own 5 V supply.

analyzer.full: Recording stopped: the capture is full. Zoom in on what you need, or clear it and record a shorter stretch.
analyzer.waiting: Recording… run the simulation to capture edges.
analyzer.empty: Pick pins and press Record. Every edge is stamped with the CPU clock (62.5 ns), so you can measure pulses to well under a microsecond.
analyzer.hint: Click the diagram to place cursor A (Shift+click: B). Arrow keys jump A to the previous or next edge; Shift+arrows move B. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan.

palette.title: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Type a command or a part name…

welcome.title: Welcome to the RoboSim editor
welcome.body: Build a circuit, write the sketch and run it — all in the browser. This short tour shows where everything is.

parts.title: Parts library
parts.body: Search in Persian or English, then click a part to add it to the circuit, or drag it onto the canvas.

circuit.title: Circuit
circuit.body: Drag parts to move them and draw wires from pin to pin. R rotates, F flips, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy parts — even into another project.

code.title: Code
code.body: Write the Arduino sketch here. Hover a function for its help, use Libraries to add an #include, and Format to tidy the code.

run.title: Run
run.body: Run compiles the sketch and starts the simulation. Step, Stop and Reset are next to it; F5 runs from anywhere.

monitor.title: Monitor
monitor.body: Serial output and the plotter, pin states, the logic analyzer and safety warnings appear here while the simulation runs.

help.title: Help is always here
help.body: Help lists every shortcut and restarts this tour. Press Ctrl+K for the command palette: every action and part by name.
